gen_risks.description: Limited capacity among financial institutions and enterprises to design, originate, appraise, and monitor green loans and sustainability-linked instruments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Component 2 technical assistance to train NAFIN and PFI staff, establish standardized MRV guidance, and support enterprise sub-project appraisal.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexican financial institutions are limited in their capacity to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans and sustainable finance products.

gen_risks.description: Risk of greenwashing or non-achievement of Sustainability Performance Targets under Sustainability-Linked Sub-loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate independent ex-ante validation and ex-post verification of Sustainability Plans and link interest rate step-downs strictly to verified outcomes.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to ex-ante validation and ex-post verification

gen_risks.description: High upfront transaction, certification, and MRV costs deterring SME participation in sustainable finance programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize ESMAP grant resources under Component 2 to subsidize early-stage validation, verification, and feasibility assessment costs for SMEs.
gen_risks.evidence: Address lengthy procedures, limited internal SME capacity, and upfront cost hurdles as these can lead to drop-offs rather than scale.

gen_risks.description: Short-term commercial bank lending structures constraining access to long-tenor investment finance required for green technologies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide blended, long-term credit lines from IBRD and CCEFCF through NAFIN to extend loan tenors matching green asset lifecycles.
gen_risks.evidence: short-term funding structures that discourage maturity extension, information asymmetries... and weak collateral recovery all constrain financial access.

gen_risks.description: Balance sheet foreign exchange exposure for NAFIN from borrowing in USD and on-lending primarily in local currency (MXN).
gen_risks.mitigation: Hedging FX exposure using Mexico's currency swap market and restricting USD lending exclusively to exporters with verified natural hedges.
gen_risks.evidence: The financing under both first and second tier will mostly be provided to BEs in local currency... NAFIN will manage the FX risk

gen_risks.description: Credit default risk of Beneficiary Enterprises and Participating Financial Institutions impacting NAFIN's portfolio quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce single-borrower exposure limits ($4M for SMEs, $20M for mid-caps), strict PFI selection criteria, and NAFIN's proven risk management framework.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second-tier operations

gen_risks.description: Implementation delays in declaring loan effectiveness due to required adoption of the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework.
gen_risks.mitigation: Advance preparation and drafting of the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework supported by a US$1 million preparation grant (GFPP).
gen_risks.evidence: Additional Conditions of Effectiveness consist of... Borrower has adopted the Project Operations Manual... and adopted Sustainable Finance Framework

gen_risks.description: Low market uptake and slow loan demand among SMEs and PFIs due to historical unfamiliarity with sustainable debt products.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct joint outreach with anchor companies and industry associations while offering time-bound pricing step-downs to catalyze early adoption.
gen_risks.evidence: Most of NAFIN’s sustainable finance programs are donor-funded and offered to SMEs through PFIs, with a mixed record of take-up.

gen_risks.description: Persistent gender gaps in formal financial access leading to low participation by women-led businesses.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a targeted gender communication campaign, define clear eligibility criteria for women-inclusive firms, and track dedicated gender indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: women-led businesses face persistent barriers to financing: only 46 percent have ever sought credit... and just 42 percent have successfully accessed it

gen_risks.description: Lack of direct procurement execution experience within NAFIN under World Bank Procurement Regulations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a qualified internal procurement specialist to the project and receive hands-on training and continuous support from World Bank procurement staff.
gen_risks.evidence: while NAFIN staff are familiar with World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes.

gen_risks.description: Financial management efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy systems and manual data consolidation across PFIs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate detailed FM workflows and standardized reporting templates into the POM, supported by supervisory reviews and targeted internal audits.
gen_risks.evidence: The main residual FM risks relate to efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation

gen_risks.description: Substantial environmental and social risks inherent in multi-tiered financial intermediary lending across diverse industrial sectors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply a ring-fenced Exclusion List excluding high-risk activities, require PFI ESMS verification (FI-1/FI-2 only), and conduct World Bank sample reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social risk is assessed as Substantial, considering the nature of the financial instruments to be used and the structure of the operation.

gen_risks.description: Severe weather events and physical climate hazards causing operational disruptions and financial distress for beneficiary firms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finance energy-reliable, water-efficient, and climate-resilient technologies under Component 1 to protect firm operational continuity.
gen_risks.evidence: For SMEs and mid-caps, these climate risks translate into increased operational costs, reduced productivity, and heightened financial distress

gen_risks.description: Stringent international ESG and disclosure demands threatening supplier exclusion from global value chains if unaddressed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated TA and sustainable sub-loans to align SME/mid-cap operations with anchor company Scope 3 and taxonomy disclosure requirements.
gen_risks.evidence: Exporters – particularly multinational firms – face increasing pressure to integrate sustainability criteria into their supply chains... Firms that do not comply risk forward-exclusion

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
